purpose: A starting subject map for a Poverty & Inequality YouTube channel. Categories organize concrete subtopics; each entry supplies an episode question, a research outline and a boundary for case selection. Counts follow the authored coverage, with no imposed topic maximum.

topics.question: Why can poverty fall while income inequality rises?
topics.coverage: Use hypothetical distributions and explicit thresholds.

topics.question: How does household size affect comparisons of living standards?
topics.coverage: Explain equivalence scales and shared costs.

topics.question: What can wealth surveys miss about the richest households?
topics.coverage: Discuss nonresponse, valuation and offshore holdings.

topics.question: How can public services change inequality beyond cash income?
topics.coverage: Map education, health and in-kind benefits.

topics.question: Why do national averages hide persistent regional deprivation?
topics.coverage: Compare spatial cost differences and population groups.

topics.question: How can a poverty program distinguish temporary relief from durable mobility?
topics.coverage: Define time horizons and outcome measures.

topics.question: How do income, wealth and multidimensional poverty measures describe different disadvantages?
topics.coverage: State thresholds and dimensions.

topics.question: Why does the UK HBAI child material-deprivation measure have a 2024 trend break?
topics.coverage: Examine the UK Department for Work and Pensions HBAI FYE 2025 release and methodology: the updated 2024 question set and simple-count deprivation rule, its combination with low-income thresholds, and the warning against directly comparing pre-2024 with post-2024 material-deprivation estimates. Separate measurement change from a causal change in living standards, with UK, survey and year limits.

topics.question: How do housing costs and labor-market segmentation constrain intergenerational mobility?
topics.coverage: Separate mechanisms and observational evidence.

topics.question: How can cash transfers and service access be compared through distributional impact analysis?
topics.coverage: Define beneficiaries, baselines and time horizons.

topics.question: Why can equal household income provide unequal living standards when disability-related costs differ?
topics.coverage: Separate additional costs, service access and equivalence-scale assumptions using hypothetical households.

topics.question: How can rural deprivation remain hidden when housing costs are lower?
topics.coverage: Compare transport, service distance, seasonal income and access rather than one income threshold.

topics.question: How does unpaid care change the time available to earn income or use public services?
topics.coverage: Map paid work, care obligations and scheduling constraints without assuming all household members share time equally.

topics.question: How can a tax reform's distributional effect change when indirect taxes and public services are included?
topics.coverage: Define households, incidence assumptions, baseline and time horizon in a transparent illustrative model.

This curriculum organizes the core disciplines of Poverty & Inequality across four progressive tiers:

   - *Question:* How did a poverty measure's purpose shape its original definition?
   - *Key Focus:* Trace one poverty or inequality measure through its original policy purpose and methodological changes; distinguish changing definitions from changing living conditions. Evidence base: Trace dated origin records and subsequent interpretations. Case records: household microdata documentation, thresholds, prices, survey weights and original policy evaluations. Starting framework: World Bank poverty measurement methodology (https://documents1.worldbank.org/curated/en/099101424092027337/pdf/P500855154ddde0b31827a1e9377c43d15e.pdf). Evidence base: Read the original evaluation and its population, comparator, outcomes and limitations. Case records: household microdata documentation, thresholds, prices, survey weights and original policy evaluations. Evidence base: Use attributable contribution records and consented participant accounts. Case records: household microdata documentation, thresholds, prices, survey weights and original policy evaluations.
